note: Guidance only. Every step is performed by you in your own account. Entries marked verified cite the platform's own documentation; everything else is generic and says so.

apply_steps: Open the original link yourself and read the full listing, including country rules, requirements and pay.
Confirm Kenya is accepted in the listing or in the platform's own country rules before spending time.
Complete the platform's profile or application using only true information.
Submit the application yourself, then record the date here.
Complete any assessment, interview or identity check yourself; never use another person or tool to impersonate you.
assessments: Read the assessment instructions fully before starting.
Do the assessment yourself, without outside help unless the instructions allow it.
after_applying: Check the platform's own status page or your email for responses.
Record any response, interview or decision here.
task_qc: Read the task instructions twice before starting.
Follow the instructions exactly; do not guess where they are unclear: look for an example or contact support.
Check spelling, formatting and length against what the task asks for.
Only submit genuine work and genuine evidence.
payout: Confirm a payout method that works from Kenya inside your own account before relying on income.
common_mistakes: Assuming a listing accepts Kenya because the site loads from Kenya.
Skipping the instructions or the examples.
Submitting work you did not check.

apply_steps: Sign in to YOUR OpenTrain account at app.opentrain.ai. You can apply only after your profile is complete (upload your real resume; add your tools, languages and experience).
Open the job from the link in this packet and read the full listing. Pay, countries and requirements come from the listing; a listing with no countries does NOT mean it is open worldwide.

Check the requirements card (All Job Requirements Met / Some Missing). Missing items are warnings: add an item to your profile only if it is true; otherwise you may still apply but be less competitive.

Location Match: your profile country must be one of the job's eligible locations. Set your real country of residence (Kenya). A location message can block the proposal and the check may ask your browser for your location; do not use a VPN.
Submit the proposal yourself, using your approved draft. If this is a PARTNER job, applying opens the source application page outside OpenTrain: finish the application on the partner's site.

If the job asks for an AI interview (text or voice), complete it yourself. For voice: quiet room, working microphone (headset best), stable connection, no VPN or strict firewall. Typical fields: LinkedIn URL, years of AI-training experience, weekly availability, previous platforms and task types: answer truthfully.
If OpenTrain asks for identity verification after you submit (Settings -> Verification; Didit or Stripe Identity, two attempts), do it yourself with a clear photo of your real ID.
Come back here and record the submission date, then watch My Proposals and Messages.
assessments: AI interview (if the job requires it): your answers go to the employer; stay consistent with your profile and draft.
Some jobs require a screening course or identity verification after you submit: both are completed by you personally.
A skills test mentioned in the listing: read the instructions in full and allow uninterrupted time.
after_applying: Proposals you send on OpenTrain show on My Proposals as Pending Review, Under Review, Shortlisted, Resume Sent, Hired, Declined or Job closed. OpenTrain cannot guarantee a response date.
The employer may Message you with questions: check Messages and reply yourself.
Partner jobs: the partner tracks your application, not OpenTrain. Check the partner's site or email and record the outcome here.
If hired, the job appears in Ongoing Jobs: open Project Instructions and Project To-dos first.
task_qc: Open the job's Project Instructions: they are the source of truth for permitted work, the tracking project and monitoring settings.
Complete every required Project To-do (they complete only when the tool confirms; you cannot tick them yourself).
If time tracking is used, set up ONLY the tool assigned to you; do not create separate accounts unless the to-do says so.
Time tracking test (Hubstaff example): run the desktop timer on the named project for at least two minutes with input tracking on; web-only or manual time does not count.
Use your OpenTrain Work Email (@opentrain.work) for project invitations; check the sender before opening any link or attachment.
Deliver the milestone work described in the contract and the published job instructions before requesting payout.
Request payout with Complete & Request Payout on a funded milestone (Active & Funded -> Pending Approval -> Paid).
payout: Set up payouts from Settings -> Payouts -> Add Payout Method. Do not create a separate account on stripe.com.
Kenya is on OpenTrain's payout-country list (checked 2026-11-08), but confirm inside your account before relying on income.
Only record money as received here after it actually reaches you.
common_mistakes: Reading an empty country list as open worldwide.
Using a VPN during location checks or voice interviews.
Creating extra accounts for time-tracking tools instead of using the assigned one.
Setting up payouts on stripe.com instead of via OpenTrain settings.
Ticking skills or experience on your profile that you do not have.

microworkers.notes: Verified only from the public FAQ and terms. Task-specific rules are shown inside each task after you log in.
apply_steps: Register yourself (free). You may keep only ONE account; duplicate accounts get terminated.
Do not use proxy servers, robots, scrapers or any automated means to access the site (terms).
Browse tasks yourself while signed in, read each task's instructions and country targeting, and accept only tasks you can complete truthfully.
After you have earned about $1.00 you will be asked for KYC verification (a valid government ID, a selfie, and a selfie with the ID): do this yourself before you can withdraw.
after_applying: Submitted tasks appear under Tasks I finished, where you can check your submitted proof and its rating.
task_qc: Read the employer's instructions fully and follow them exactly before submitting proof.
If a task needs revision you get 48 hours; a task not revised after 48 hours is automatically set to NOK (unpaid).
Submit genuine proof of work you actually did; never fabricate or duplicate proof, and never submit the same job twice from another account.
Check the task's country targeting and any special requirements before starting.
payout: You can only request a withdrawal once you reach the minimum amount and have completed KYC; withdrawal methods vary by country (for example Transpay is not available everywhere): check the options inside your own account.
Only record money as received here after it actually reaches you.
common_mistakes: Creating a second account.
Using a proxy or VPN to reach the site.
Ignoring the 48-hour revision window.
Skipping KYC and then being unable to withdraw.

handshake_ai.notes: Verified only from the public terms. Role-specific requirements and work authorization are shown on each opportunity page.
apply_steps: Create your account yourself. You may hold only ONE account; do not create accounts with scripts, bots or crawlers.
Open the opportunity page yourself and read the requirements, location and work-authorization notes before applying.
Apply with truthful profile information and keep your details accurate and up to date (terms).
Complete any assessment or interview yourself.
after_applying: Check your Handshake AI account and email for responses, then record them here.
task_qc: Follow the project's published instructions exactly.
Never copy or bulk-collect listing data with scripts (prohibited).
common_mistakes: Creating a second account if the first is suspended.
Using scripts to gather opportunity data.

braintrust.notes: Verified only from the public terms. Kenya is not named as restricted; role-specific limits and payout method are unverified.
apply_steps: Create your talent profile yourself with truthful information only.
Open each role from its own page and check its requirements and location before applying.
Complete any vetting, certification or interview yourself.
Do not use a VPN to get around a territory restriction.
after_applying: Check your Braintrust dashboard and email for responses, then record them here.
task_qc: Never falsify hours, keystrokes or mouse activity recorded for billing; never bill time you did not work (talent terms).
Never misrepresent your experience, skills or another person's profile as your own.
Deliver what the client's contract states and keep communication on the platform.
payout: Confirm in your own account which payout methods are available in Kenya before relying on income.
common_mistakes: Overstating experience on the profile.
Logging time that was not worked.

rapidworkers.notes: Verified only from the public FAQ and terms; the Acceptable Use and Anti-Spam policies were not read.
apply_steps: Sign up yourself (free for workers, no upfront fees to join).
Read each task's checklist and country targeting before starting.
SKIP social-engagement tasks (buying or posting likes, views, follows, votes or fake reviews): they are engagement manipulation and are not part of this project.
after_applying: After you submit proof, the employer reviews it; the FAQ says most approvals happen within 24-48 hours depending on the campaign.
task_qc: If your proof does not match the employer's instructions it can be rejected and unpaid: read the checklist before submitting.
Submit only genuine proof.
payout: Confirm payout options inside your own account before relying on income.
common_mistakes: Doing engagement-manipulation tasks.
Submitting proof that does not match the checklist.

atlas_capture.notes: The official Opportunities page states an iPhone 11 or newer is required. This work is NOT available on an Android phone such as the Samsung A05.
apply_steps: Do not pursue this platform unless you obtain a supported iPhone 11 or newer: the work is filming everyday tasks with an iPhone, so an Android phone does not qualify.
task_qc: Recordings must be genuine and made by you; never fabricate or fake recordings.
common_mistakes: Trying to use an unsupported device.
Buying equipment before confirming country availability and pay.
